headline: Record quarter drives raised full-year growth targets
summary_short: Cboe reported record net revenue (revenues less cost of revenues) of $731.6M, up 24.6% y/y, and diluted EPS of $3.35, up 50% y/y, then raised its FY2026 organic net revenue growth target to 'mid to high teens' from 'low double-digit to mid teens'.
summary_long: Net revenue rose 24.6% y/y to a record $731.6M, with growth across every segment — Options net revenue hit $473.9M (+30% y/y) on a 26% rise in options ADV; N.A. Equities, Europe/APAC and Global FX each grew double digits. Diluted EPS of $3.35 rose 50% y/y as revenue growth outpaced a 3% rise in operating expenses. Cboe raised its FY2026 organic net-revenue growth target to 'mid to high teens' from 'low double-digit to mid teens', raised Data Vantage growth guidance to 'low teens', and raised capex guidance to $98-108M from $73-83M. Cash stood at $2,276.2M.

'Total revenue' above is GAAP gross revenue (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerIncludingAssessedTax, SEC-verbatim); Cboe's own headline metric is 'net revenue' (revenues less cost of revenues), shown separately at $731.6M / +24.6% y/y, matching the release's own +25% framing. The y/y jump in total cash (+81.2%) is not explained in the release and is not asserted as a driver.

drivers.explanation: Broad-based growth across all net-revenue captions; Options net revenue set a record on a 26% rise in total options ADV and a 6% increase in options revenue per contract.
Operating expenses rose only 3%, as higher severance and bonus accruals were mostly offset by the absence of 2025's Cboe Japan impairment charge, letting revenue growth flow through.
EPS growth tracked net-income growth; a lower effective tax rate (28.6% vs. 29.7% a year ago), tied to reduced interest on resolved uncertain tax positions, added a modest tailwind.
Citing strong first-half momentum and record derivatives volumes, Cboe raised its FY2026 organic net-revenue growth target to 'mid to high teens' and its Data Vantage growth target to 'low teens'.
